items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: He'd hold his daddy's horn under one hand when we wasn't playing, and under his arm, and he'd hold mine under the other.

ctx.x: Oven-Algeous. You heard of Henry? Yes. That was Henry Allen, young Henry Allen's father.

Yeah, that was his father. Oh, yeah. And his son, the one that's playing now, used to walk between us and hold both of us's horn under one arm. He'd hold his daddy's horn under one hand when we wasn't playing, and under his arm, and he'd hold mine under the other. He was about nine years old then, see? And after I played over there, and then we got all that work from Seussbury, Protection Levy, all of that, see? And all the summer long we were just playing parades up there for different lodges.
